title: Padua cathedral Eucharistic rubrics and Roman Mass-book witnesses

traditions.label: Padua cathedral rubrics and Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: Named Eucharistic rubrics in local cathedral ordinal E.57 and identified chant loci of Roman Missal D.30; the books do not define a continuous independent Padua recension.
traditions.coverage_note: Two bounded manuscript states supported by inspected studies and official descriptions; original full manuscripts, complete texts, revisions and adoption remain open.

sources.title: ISEP, 2002 E.57 critical edition and facsimile publisher record
sources.inspection: Entire publisher HTML acquired and read. Identifies Padua Chapter E.57 as thirteenth century and the two-volume 2002 edition, studies and full facsimile.
sources.limitations: Publication metadata only; the complete 2002 edition and original manuscript are not acquired.

sources.title: Claudio Bellinati, Contributo alla storia della cattedrale di Padova (2014)
sources.inspection: Complete 201-page publisher-linked PDF acquired. Printed pp. 26–29, 43–45, 56, 74–79 inspected; pp. 44, 77–78 checked against page images (PDF pp. 76, 109–110). Read named E.57 Mass/communion loci and D.30 dating/1350 inventory identification.
sources.limitations: Scholarly manuscript and archival description, not inspection of original E.57 leaves or Inventario 1350; the book index calls D.30 a breviary although its p. 44 body calls it a missal, so that index label is not adopted.

sources.title: Francesca Leto, La liturgia iconica degli spazi della Cappella degli Scrovegni e del Battistero di Padova (2025)
sources.inspection: Complete 150-page university volume acquired; chapter pp. 86–88 read, pp. 87–88 checked against page images (PDF pp. 88–89), including E.57 edited loci 127g and 140e in notes 55 and 59.
sources.limitations: Exact scholarly references to E.57, not original manuscript collation. The chapter also uses a separate Franciscan Missal MFR; its prayer texts are not transferred to E.57. First edition is 2025, despite the download URL's 2026 directory.

sources.title: Diego Toigo, Intonazioni monodiche della Passione in Italia fra i secoli XIII e XVI, doctoral dissertation
sources.inspection: Whole 228-page dissertation acquired. Printed pp. 47–48 read; p. 48 and its D.30 original manuscript crop checked against image (PDF p. 86). D.30 is identified as Missale Romanum, with Matthew Passion melody c. 70r/v and Mark c. 74r/v.
sources.limitations: Only the reproduced short musical crop is directly visible; complete original leaves and Mass prayers remain uninspected. Early-fourteenth-century description does not resolve Bellinati's post-1323 date against IRHT's 1301–1310.

sources.title: Diocese of Padua, Ecce advenit exhibition list, 21 December 2021
sources.inspection: Entire two-page official PDF read. Item 13 identifies fourteenth-century Padua D.30 f. 20v, Epiphany introit Ecce advenit; item 4 identifies D.34 as Paris 1281–1292 Franciscan Missal.
sources.limitations: Exhibition catalogue describes the leaves; it does not display their original full text or establish a Padua diocesan recension.

sources.title: Anna Vildera, Formulari processionali per il canto del Vangelo Liber generationis (2013)
sources.inspection: Whole 17-page article acquired; printed pp. 139 and 153 read. Identifies E.57 c. 43v with date c. 1256–1275; the cited rubric belongs to Christmas Matins.
sources.limitations: The Matins rubric is used only for identity and dating, not as an E.57 Mass proper; complete manuscript and dating argument are uninspected.

sources.title: IRHT Iter liturgicum italicum, Padova D.30, manuscript 616628
sources.inspection: Preserved complete 2026-10-19 HTML read at lines 64–85: D.30, Missale Calendarium, date 1301–1310, 360 leaves, origin Padova. Live retrieval on 2026-10-20 did not finish and was stopped; no new live verification is asserted.
sources.limitations: Catalogue dating conflicts with Bellinati 2014 p. 44's post-1323 date. Original colophon/calendar and Bernardinello 2007 I pp. 574–577 are still needed.

stages.label: Padua E.57 cathedral Eucharistic rubrics
stages.date_label: Thirteenth-century manuscript, publisher dating; narrower scholarly ranges remain qualified
stages.scope: Cathedral order-book rubrics for the Thursday Mass and reservation, Friday communion, and processions before Easter and Ascension Masses, as described at named manuscript and edition loci.
stages.witness_label: Padova, Biblioteca Capitolare, E.57, Liber ordinarius ecclesie Paduane
stages.summary: Inspected manuscript studies identify actual local cathedral Eucharistic instructions in E.57. Bellinati describes Thursday Mass and reserved consecrated bread, then the Friday celebrant's communion. Leto identifies Easter and Ascension processions before solemn Mass at exact E.57 edition loci.

evidence.claim: Identifies the local cathedral E.57 manuscript and thirteenth-century date; 2002 is the modern edition date.

evidence.locus: pp. 77–78 nn. 31, 34, citing E.57 ff. 89v–92v and 92v–95r
evidence.claim: The named ordinal contains Eucharistic instructions concerning Thursday Mass/reservation and Friday communion, in the cathedral setting.

evidence.locus: pp. 87–88 nn. 55, 59; E.57 edited sections 127g and 140e
evidence.claim: Identifies processions before the Easter Missa maior and Ascension solemn Mass in the local ordinal.

stages.limitations: Evidence is scholarly description of specified rubrics. No full original E.57 leaves, complete 2002 edition, new literal transcription, complete Missal, separate promulgation, uniform diocesan use or textual transition is established. Vildera 2013 reports c. 1256–1275 and Leto 2025 gives broader 1234–1304; the century coordinate follows the publisher and is not a duration of use.
stages.reception: The witness is explicitly the Padua cathedral's local order book, with local offices, altars and ritual duties; broader parish implementation and first use remain unproved.

stages.label: Padua D.30 Roman Missal: identified chant loci
stages.date_label: Fourteenth-century witness; IRHT 1301–1310 versus Bellinati post-1323 unresolved
stages.scope: Named Epiphany introit leaf and Matthew/Mark Passion chant loci of one Roman Missal, with a reproduced short Matthew manuscript excerpt.
stages.summary: The official diocesan catalogue identifies Ecce advenit on f. 20v. Toigo identifies Roman Missal D.30's Matthew and Mark Passion melodies at ff. 70 and 74 and reproduces a short manuscript crop. Bellinati associates this missal with the cathedral's 1350 inventory.

evidence.claim: D.30 f. 20v contains the Epiphany introit Ecce advenit and is described as a fourteenth-century Padua missal.

evidence.locus: pp. 47–48, n. 153 and manuscript crop on p. 48
evidence.claim: Identifies D.30 as a Roman Missal and specifies Matthew/Mark Passion melody loci.
Identifies D.30 as a missal later than 1323 and in the cathedral's 1350 inventory.

evidence.locus: Date and origin fields, preserved HTML lines 64–85
evidence.claim: Records the competing 1301–1310 catalogue dating and Padua origin, requiring an explicit dating gap.

stages.limitations: The copying date remains unpositioned because the specific sources disagree. This is an identified Roman Mass-book witness and scoped chant description, not a complete independently reconstructed Padua Mass, a distinct local recension, or verified altar use.
stages.reception: Padua origin and cathedral ownership are described; the specific liturgical use and first celebration are not established by custody.

gaps.period: Thirteenth-century ordinal and its later layers
gaps.missing: Complete original E.57 Eucharistic leaves, editorial layer distinctions, exact prayers and full local adoption evidence.
gaps.next_source: Acquire Cattin/Vildera 2002 critical edition and full facsimile: E.57 ff. 1r–7v, 89v–95r; edited sections 127g, 140e. Inspect dating discussion and separate original text from corrections. No public full facsimile obtained in this pass.
gaps.consequence: The bounded local rubrical state is documented through studies, with no whole-book transcription, new normative station, transition or text inheritance.

gaps.missing: Resolution of 1301–1310 versus post-1323/c. 1338 dating, complete calendar/colophon, original Mass prayers, and actual local use.
gaps.next_source: Bernardinello 2007 I pp. 574–577; La miniatura a Padova 1999 pp. 98–99; D.30 f. 20v, 70r/v, 74r/v and calendar; Cathedral Inventario 1350 f. 14v. Compare the original manuscript and calendar layers before restoring narrow numeric dates.
gaps.consequence: D.30 stays unpositioned; ownership and a Roman Missal identity do not create a separate Padua recension.

gaps.period: Medieval local books, Roman reception and later holdings
gaps.missing: Exact Mass components and reception of B.26, B.31 and C.47/D.34; older and newer ordinal relation; fully evidenced local sequence and later adoption.
gaps.next_source: Inspect B.26, Roman-Franciscan B.31 (reported colophon 5 October 1328), surviving C.47/D.34 Cholet volumes and their lost third volume; distinguish lost Rubricarium ministrorum altaris recorded in 1407 from extant E.57. Read original 1339/1350 book inventories before asserting a Romanization transition.
gaps.consequence: No inferred ancestry, universal substitution date or complete local Mass follows from date order, a Padua shelfmark, Franciscan copying or Pataviense naming Passau.
